note: All four source drafts feed one campaign, so they share one target output. Grade conformance against target_output, violation detection against expected_violations, and fact checking against campaign_facts. campaign_facts uses the flat 15-field runtime schema shared by extract.md, conform.md, grade.md, and the app form. All paths are relative to the repo root and listed in file_map.

campaign_facts.unchanged_items: Driver Vehicle Inspection Report submission standards

target_output.preview_text: A required 20-minute module is due 26 September
target_output.body:
We are changing how we calculate the Safety Performance Index (SPI). The revised scoring model takes effect **1 October**. All Partners must complete a required training module by **26 September**.

We recalibrated the model after our most recent network review. Following-distance and hours-of-service events now carry more weight. Hard-braking events carry less, because the previous weighting produced false positives for Partners running dense metro lanes.

Threshold changes:

- Tier 1 moves from 92 to 94
- Tier 2 moves from 85 to 88
- Tier 3 stays at 78

We calculate scores on a rolling 90-day window. The current window runs 1 July through 30 September.

We will not rescore past performance under the revised model. Your first score under the new weighting publishes 15 October.

The Partner Learning Center (PLC) module covers the recalibration method, how to read the revised scorecard, and what drives each weighted component. It runs 20 minutes.

If we have not recorded your completion, we hold you at your current tier until we do. That affects Load Acceptance Rate (LAR) prioritization.

Driver Vehicle Inspection Report submission standards do not change.

Complete the module by **26 September**.

spec_gaps_found.gap: Tier labels are numbers under 10 and F-05 does not say whether Tier 1 or Tier one is correct.
spec_gaps_found.resolution: Add F-12: tier designations are proper nouns and always use numerals.
spec_gaps_found.why_it_matters: Without this the grader guesses, and it will guess differently across runs.

spec_gaps_found.gap: T-04 requires first-use expansion but does not say whether the subject line counts as first use.
spec_gaps_found.resolution: Add T-10: subject line and preview text are excluded from first-use expansion. Body counts as first use.
spec_gaps_found.why_it_matters: S-01 caps the subject at 50 characters, which makes expansion in a subject line effectively impossible.

spec_gaps_found.gap: R-02 requires footer block 4.2, which contains 'TPN operational email', creating a first-use expansion conflict with T-04.
spec_gaps_found.resolution: Add R-07: the standard footer block is exempt from Section 2 terminology rules.
spec_gaps_found.why_it_matters: Every email would otherwise fail T-04 by way of its own required footer.
